1.web: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
1.asv: I made a covenant with mine eyes; How then should I look upon a virgin?

2.web: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
2.asv: For what is the portion from God above, And the heritage from the Almighty on high?

3.web: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?
3.asv: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, And disaster to the workers of iniquity?

4.web: Doesn’t he see my ways, and number all my steps?
4.asv: Doth not he see my ways, And number all my steps?

5.web: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit
5.asv: If I have walked with falsehood, And my foot hath hasted to deceit

6.web: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
6.asv: (Let me be weighed in an even balance, That God may know mine integrity);

7.web: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
7.asv: If my step hath turned out of the way, And my heart walked after mine eyes, And if any spot hath cleaved to my hands:

8.web: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
8.asv: Then let me sow, and let another eat; Yea, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

9.web: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
9.asv: If my heart hath been enticed unto a woman, And I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door;

10.web: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
10.asv: Then let my wife grind unto another, And let others bow down upon her.

11.web: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges:
11.asv: For that were a heinous crime; Yea, it were an iniquity to be punished by the judges:

12.web: For it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
12.asv: For it is a fire that consumeth unto Destruction, And would root out all mine increase.

13.web: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me;
13.asv: If I have despised the cause of my man-servant or of my maid-servant, When they contended with me;

14.web: What then shall I do when God rises up? When he visits, what shall I answer him?
14.asv: What then shall I do when God riseth up? And when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

15.web: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?
15.asv: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? And did not one fashion us in the womb?

16.web: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
16.asv: If I have withheld the poor fromtheirdesire, Or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

17.web: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it
17.asv: Or have eaten my morsel alone, And the fatherless hath not eaten thereof

18.web: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, her have I guided from my mother’s womb);
18.asv: (Nay, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, And her have I guided from my mother’s womb);

19.web: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;
19.asv: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, Or that the needy had no covering;

20.web: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
20.asv: If his loins have not blessed me, And if he hath not been warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

21.web: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,
21.asv: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, Because I saw my help in the gate:

22.web: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
22.asv: Then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder-blade, And mine arm be broken from the bone.

23.web: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because his majesty, I can do nothing.
23.asv: For calamity from God is a terror to me, And by reason of his majesty I can do nothing.

24.web: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’
24.asv: If I have made gold my hope, And have said to the fine gold, Thou artmy confidence;

25.web: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;
25.asv: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gotten much;

26.web: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,
26.asv: If I have beheld the sun when it shined, Or the moon walking in brightness,

27.web: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
27.asv: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, And my mouth hath kissed my hand:

28.web: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God who is above.
28.asv: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judges; For I should have denied the God that is above.

29.web: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him;
29.asv: If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, Or lifted up myself when evil found him

30.web: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
30.asv: (Yea, I have not suffered my mouth to sin By asking his life with a curse);

31.web: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’
31.asv: If the men of my tent have not said, Who can find one that hath not been filled with his meat?

32.web: (the foreigner has not lodged in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
32.asv: (The sojourner hath not lodged in the street; But I have opened my doors to the traveller);

33.web: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
33.asv: If like Adam I have covered my transgressions, By hiding mine iniquity in my bosom,

34.web: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—
34.asv: Because I feared the great multitude, And the contempt of families terrified me, So that I kept silence, and went not out of the door—

35.web: oh that I had one to hear me! (behold, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me); let the accuser write my indictment!
35.asv: Oh that I had one to hear me! (Lo, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me) Andthat I hadthe indictment which mine adversary hath written!

36.web: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.
36.asv: Surely I would carry it upon my shoulder; I would bind it unto me as a crown:

37.web: I would declare to him the number of my steps. as a prince would I go near to him.
37.asv: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; As a prince would I go near unto him.

38.web: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
38.asv: If my land crieth out against me, And the furrows thereof weep together;

39.web: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,
39.asv: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, Or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

40.web: let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
40.asv: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, And cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
